```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE, fig.path = "figures/results-", dpi = 110)
pkgload::load_all("pmxlandscape", quiet = TRUE)
pct <- function(x, digits = 0) paste0(formatC(100 * x, format = "f", digits = digits), "%")

software <- read.csv("taxonomy/software.csv", colClasses = "character")
estimation <- software$family[software$group == "estimation"]

# The review record, with the revisions decided since on the same review text (for example the
# reviewer running the applicant's model in a tool)
fdaRevisions <- read.csv("sources/fda/results/record_revisions.csv", colClasses = "character")
fdaReview <- fdaApplyRevisions(fdaReadResults("sources/fda"), fdaRevisions)
# Drugs whose review names no tool: evidence from the submission's other documents (other FDA
# reviews, EMA assessment reports), applied on top of the review record
fdaOther <- read.csv("sources/fda/other_reviews/decisions.csv", colClasses = "character")
fda <- fdaApplyOtherEvidence(fdaReview, fdaOther)
nReviewNotStated <- sum(fdaReview$category == "popPK present, software not stated")
fdaTab <- fdaToolTable(fda)
fdaSum <- fdaSummary("sources/fda", results = fda)$sponsorByYear
count <- function(label) fdaSum$All[fdaSum$sponsor_category == label]

lit <- read.csv("sources/literature/results/shares.csv")
litInfo <- readLines("sources/literature/results/run_info.txt")
litDate <- sub("run_date: ", "", litInfo[1])
# Papers naming each tool: the taxonomy patterns on the local corpus (local_search.R), every paper
# of 2021 to 2026 found by the term route (the core and the extension) or the tool route
# (development run, 2026-10-21)
litAll <- read.csv(gzfile("sources/literature/results/ids_local_all.csv.gz"), colClasses = "character")
litAll$year <- as.integer(litAll$year)
litAll <- litAll[litAll$year >= 2021, ]
litIds <- litAll[c("source", "year", "software", "id")]
# Every paper was read for a model fit of its own (relevance codebook version 2); only papers read
# as own_fit count
litRel <- read.csv("classifications/lit_relevance/decisions_v2.csv", colClasses = "character")
litRel$source <- c("PubMed" = "PubMed (title/abstract)", "Europe PMC" = "Europe PMC (full text)")[litRel$source]
litBase <- litAll[litAll$software == "All (base set)", ]
litBase$value <- litRel$value[match(paste(litBase$source, litBase$id), paste(litRel$source, litRel$item_id))]
litBase$value[is.na(litBase$value)] <- "no text"
litBase$route <- ifelse(litBase$tool_route == "", "term", ifelse(litBase$admitted == "tool", "tool", "both"))
litExclude <- litBase$id[litBase$value != "own_fit"]
litRelCheck <- read.csv("classifications/lit_relevance/checks_v2.csv")
litShares <- literatureShares(litIds, estimation, exclude = litExclude, excludeNamed = TRUE)
# Papers using each tool: the tool use classification (classifications/tool_use)
toolTags <- read.csv("classifications/tool_use/tags.csv", colClasses = "character")
toolCheck <- read.csv("classifications/tool_use/checks.csv")
toolRuns <- read.csv("classifications/tool_use/runs.csv")
litUsedShares <- literatureShares(literatureUsedIds(litIds, toolTags), estimation, exclude = litExclude, excludeNamed = TRUE)
epBase0 <- length(unique(litIds$id[litIds$source == "Europe PMC (full text)" & litIds$software == "All (base set)"]))
anyTool <- unique(litShares[c("source", "year", "n_any", "base_n")])
anyShare <- tapply(anyTool$n_any, anyTool$source, sum) / tapply(anyTool$base_n, anyTool$source, sum)
pmAff <- read.csv("sources/literature/results/pubmed_affiliations.csv", colClasses = "character")
pmGroup <- ifelse(pmAff$affiliation_type %in% c("industry", "CRO"), "sponsor",
  ifelse(pmAff$affiliation_type == "academia", "academia", NA)
)
names(pmGroup) <- pmAff$pmid
litAff <- literatureShares(litIds[litIds$source == "PubMed (title/abstract)", ], estimation,
  group = pmGroup[!is.na(pmGroup)], exclude = litExclude, excludeNamed = TRUE
)

xc <- read.csv("sources/fda/crosscheck/results/crosscheck_drugs.csv", colClasses = "character")
# the cross-check table copies the record as it was; take the category and tool from the revised one
xc$category <- fdaReview$category[match(xc$application, fdaReview$application)]
xc$sponsor_tool_family <- fdaReview$sponsor_tool_family[match(xc$application, fdaReview$application)]
notStated <- xc[xc$category == "popPK present, software not stated" & !xc$application %in% fdaOther$application, ]
likely <- notStated[notStated$evidence == "sponsor paper near submission", ]
noEvidence <- notStated[notStated$evidence == "none", ]
valid <- xc[startsWith(xc$category, "Tool stated") & xc$evidence == "sponsor paper near submission", ]

# One count table per source or group: totals, items naming a tool, each family
countTable <- function(s, total, totalLabel, anyLabel = "Naming an estimation tool") {
  s <- s[s$n > 0 | ave(s$n, s$family, FUN = sum) > 0, ]
  s$total <- s[[total]]
  knitr::kable(shareTable(s, totalLabel = totalLabel, anyLabel = anyLabel), align = paste0("l", strrep("r", length(unique(s$year)))))
}

pageFile <- "sources/page/results/page_abstracts.csv"
page <- if (file.exists(pageFile)) read.csv(pageFile) else NULL
pageReady <- !is.null(page) && !any(page$estimation_source == "pending")
# Only the tools an abstract used count: the tool use classification drops comparators and
# passing mentions. The analysis types still come from the earlier role reading (pageRoleCheck)
pageRoleCheck <- read.csv("sources/page/results/role_check.csv")
pageNamed <- pageToolUse(page, toolTags, used = FALSE)
page <- pageToolUse(page, toolTags)
```

# Estimation software: detailed results

PMx Landscape first measures which estimation software is used for population pharmacokinetic
and related model-based analyses. This document gives the detailed results of that measure, source
by source, with their methods, tables and charts, followed by the first analyses built on the
measure and a first look at machine learning and AI. The project and its method are summarised in
the [README](../../README.md), and terms used in a specific sense are defined in the
[glossary](../glossary.md).

```{r results-setup, include = FALSE}
# A table folded by default, placed right after the paragraph that refers to it
folded <- function(summary, tab) {
  knitr::asis_output(paste0(
    "<details>\n<summary>", summary, "</summary>\n\n", paste(tab, collapse = "\n"), "\n\n</details>\n"
  ))
}
# Share of each family pooled over the years of one source or group: items naming it / items naming any tool
pooled <- function(d, key = "family") {
  den <- sum(unique(d[c("year", "n_any")])$n_any)
  sort(tapply(d$n, d[[key]], sum) / den, decreasing = TRUE)
}
andList <- function(x) if (length(x) <= 1) paste(x) else paste(paste(x[-length(x)], collapse = ", "), "and", x[length(x)])

# FDA
withLikely <- table(c(fda$sponsor_tool_family[startsWith(fda$category, "Tool stated")], likely$inferred))
fdaPatterns <- readPatterns("sources/fda/config/patterns.json")
fdaSearched <- unique(sub(" (name expanded)", "", fdaPatterns$name[fdaPatterns$group == "estimation"], fixed = TRUE))
fdaUnused <- setdiff(fdaSearched, fdaTab$family)
fdaYears <- as.character(2021:2025)
notStatedYear <- unlist(fdaSum[fdaSum$sponsor_category == "popPK present, software not stated", fdaYears]) /
  unlist(fdaSum[fdaSum$sponsor_category == "Total", fdaYears])
nTemplate <- sum(fda$evidence_strength == "indirect, template phrase only")
likelyTab <- sort(table(likely$inferred), decreasing = TRUE)

# Literature
pmShare <- pooled(litShares[litShares$source == "PubMed (title/abstract)", ], "software")
epShare <- pooled(litShares[litShares$source == "Europe PMC (full text)", ], "software")
top3 <- c("NONMEM", "Monolix", "Phoenix NLME")
litRestMax <- max(pmShare[setdiff(names(pmShare), top3)], epShare[setdiff(names(epShare), top3)])
affGroups <- c(sponsor = "sponsor", academia = "academia")
litAffShare <- lapply(affGroups, function(g) pooled(litAff[litAff$group == g, ], "software"))
litAffN <- vapply(affGroups, function(g) sum(unique(litAff[litAff$group == g, c("year", "n_any")])$n_any), numeric(1))
pmUsed <- pooled(litUsedShares[litUsedShares$source == "PubMed (title/abstract)", ], "software")
epUsed <- pooled(litUsedShares[litUsedShares$source == "Europe PMC (full text)", ], "software")
usedTool <- unique(litUsedShares[c("source", "year", "n_any", "base_n")])
usedAny <- tapply(usedTool$n_any, usedTool$source, sum) / tapply(usedTool$base_n, usedTool$source, sum)

# PAGE
sharesAll <- pageShares(page)
shares <- sharesAll[sharesAll$year >= 2016, ]
recent <- page[page$year >= 2016, ]
nDemo <- sum(recent$software_demo)
years <- range(recent$year)
nAbs <- sum(!recent$software_demo & recent$estimation_source != "unknown")
nAny <- sum(!recent$software_demo & recent$estimation_source %in% c("abstract", "pdf"))
recentNamed <- pageNamed[pageNamed$year >= 2016 & !pageNamed$software_demo, ]
nNamed <- sum(recentNamed$estimation_source %in% c("abstract", "pdf"))
rc <- function(m) pageRoleCheck[pageRoleCheck$measure == m, ]
pageOldTab <- read.csv("classifications/tool_use/old_comparison.csv")
pageOld <- list(share = sum(pageOldTab$Freq[as.character(pageOldTab$old) == as.character(pageOldTab$new)]) / sum(pageOldTab$Freq))
affTab <- sort(table(recent$affiliation_type[!recent$software_demo]), decreasing = TRUE)
pgShare <- pooled(shares[shares$group == "all", ])
pgYear <- function(f, y) shares$share[shares$group == "all" & shares$family == f & shares$year == y]
pgAffShare <- lapply(affGroups, function(g) pooled(shares[shares$group == g, ]))
pgRestMax <- max(pgShare[setdiff(names(pgShare), c("NONMEM", "Monolix", "nlmixr", "Stan/Torsten"))])

# Analysis types
readTypes <- function(f) {
  d <- read.csv(f, colClasses = "character")
  d$year <- as.integer(d$year)
  d$types <- lapply(strsplit(d$types, "; ", fixed = TRUE), function(x) x[x != ""])
  d
}
atItems <- readTypes("analysis/analysis_types/results/items.csv")
fdaAt <- readTypes("analysis/analysis_types/results/fda_items.csv")
checks <- read.csv("analysis/analysis_types/results/checks.csv")
litCheck <- checks[checks$check == "second reading check (fresh sample)", ]
fdaCheck <- checks[checks$classifier == "reading", ]
spreadOf <- function(d, mode, label) {
  d$types <- lumpTypes(d$types, mode)
  a <- typeByTool(d)
  a <- a[a$tool == "All", ]
  data.frame(source = label, type = a$type, share = a$share, n = a$n, n_tool = a$n_tool)
}
pageAt <- atItems[atItems$source == "PAGE" & atItems$year >= 2016, ]
spread <- rbind(
  spreadOf(pageAt, "detailed", sprintf("PAGE 2016 to 2026\n(%d)", nrow(pageAt))),
  spreadOf(atItems[atItems$source == "Europe PMC", ], "detailed", sprintf("Europe PMC\n(%d)", sum(atItems$source == "Europe PMC"))),
  spreadOf(atItems[atItems$source == "PubMed", ], "simple", sprintf("PubMed\n(%d)", sum(atItems$source == "PubMed"))),
  spreadOf(fdaAt, "simple", sprintf("FDA reviews\n(%d)", nrow(fdaAt)))
)
pageLumped <- pageAt
pageLumped$types <- lumpTypes(pageLumped$types, "detailed")
liftTools <- c("NONMEM", "Monolix", "nlmixr", "Pumas", "Stan/Torsten")
lift <- typeLift(pageLumped)
lift <- lift[lift$tool %in% liftTools, ]
lift <- lift[order(match(lift$tool, liftTools), match(lift$type, lumpedTypes)), ]
fdaPkOnly <- mean(vapply(fdaAt$types, function(x) identical(x, "PK only"), logical(1)))
pagePkOnly <- spread$share[startsWith(spread$source, "PAGE") & spread$type == "PK only"]
shortType <- stats::setNames(c(
  "PK only", "PK/PD or exposure-response", "non-continuous endpoints or time-to-event",
  "full Bayesian models", "machine learning", "QSP or PBPK"
), lumpedTypes)
leanList <- function(t, dir) {
  x <- lift[lift$tool == t & !is.na(lift$ratio) & (if (dir == "over") lift$lower > 1 else lift$upper < 1), ]
  unname(shortType[x$type])
}
toolBullet <- function(t) {
  o <- leanList(t, "over")
  u <- leanList(t, "under")
  paste0(
    "- **", t, "** leans towards ", if (length(o)) andList(o) else "no type",
    if (length(u)) paste0(", and away from ", andList(u)) else "", "."
  )
}
maTool <- read.csv("analysis/analysis_types/results/page_methods_applied.csv")
maTool <- maTool[maTool$by == "tool" & maTool$year >= 2016, ]
methShare <- tapply(maTool$methods, maTool$group, sum) / tapply(maTool$methods + maTool$applied, maTool$group, sum)
nTool <- stats::setNames(lift$n_tool[match(liftTools, lift$tool)], liftTools)
liftN <- function(t, ty) lift$n[lift$tool == t & lift$type == ty]

# Lag
sponsor <- sharesAll[sharesAll$group == "sponsor", ]
fdaCounts <- fdaToolCounts(fda)
trend <- fitTrend(sponsor, "NONMEM")
lags <- 0:15
profile <- estimateLag(fdaCounts, trend, lags = lags)
best <- profile$lag[which.max(profile$loglik)]
plausible <- profile$lag[profile$rel_lik > 0.15]
atEdge <- best %in% range(lags)
slope <- stats::coef(trend$fit)[["year"]]
pageLevel <- stats::plogis(stats::predict(trend$fit, newdata = data.frame(year = c(2016, 2026))))
fdaLevel <- sum(fdaCounts$n[fdaCounts$family == "NONMEM"]) / sum(fdaCounts$n_any[fdaCounts$family == "NONMEM"])
pageYears <- range(sponsor$year)
crossYear <- (stats::qlogis(fdaLevel) - stats::coef(trend$fit)[[1]]) / slope
projected <- projectShares(trend, best, c(2030, 2026 + best))
pageNm <- sponsor[sponsor$family == "NONMEM", ]
fdaNm <- fdaCounts[fdaCounts$family == "NONMEM", ]

# Methodology to applied
ma <- read.csv("analysis/analysis_types/results/page_methods_applied.csv")
maGroups <- c("Monolix", "BUGS", "nlmixr", "Pumas", "Stan/Torsten")
maTools <- ma[ma$by == "tool" & ma$group %in% maGroups, ]
maMl <- ma[ma$by == "type" & ma$group == "Machine learning, AI, neural ODEs", ]
maMl$group <- "Machine learning, AI (any tool)"
maPlot <- rbind(maTools, maMl)
methodShare <- function(g) {
  d <- maPlot[maPlot$group == g & maPlot$methods + maPlot$applied > 0, ]
  first <- head(d, 4)
  last <- d[d$year >= 2023, ]
  list(
    firstYears = range(first$year), nFirst = sum(first$methods + first$applied),
    first = sum(first$methods) / sum(first$methods + first$applied),
    last = sum(last$methods) / sum(last$methods + last$applied), nLast = sum(last$methods + last$applied)
  )
}
ms <- lapply(stats::setNames(unique(maPlot$group), unique(maPlot$group)), methodShare)
```

## FDA reviews of new drugs, 2021 to 2025

**In short.**

- NONMEM is the sponsor's tool for `r pct(fdaTab$share[1])` of the
  `r sum(fdaTab$drugs)` drugs with an identifiable tool.
- The other drugs with an identifiable tool use `r andList(fdaTab$family[-1])`.
  No other estimation tool searched for is the sponsor's tool for any drug.
- No document names the software for `r pct(nrow(notStated) / count("Total"))`
  of the `r count("Total")` approvals.
- In 2021 the software is still not named for `r pct(notStatedYear[["2021"]])`
  of the approvals. In later years the share is `r pct(min(notStatedYear[-1]))`
  to `r pct(max(notStatedYear[-1]))`.
- The sponsor's own papers give a likely tool for `r nrow(likely)` of the
  `r nrow(notStated)` drugs without a named tool. Adding these likely tools
  `r if (pct(fdaTab$share[1]) == pct(withLikely[["NONMEM"]] / sum(withLikely))) paste("leaves NONMEM's share at", pct(fdaTab$share[1])) else paste("moves NONMEM's share from", pct(fdaTab$share[1]), "to", pct(withLikely[["NONMEM"]] / sum(withLikely)))`.

**Methods.** The drugs counted are the novel drug approvals of 2021 to 2025 by
the FDA's Center for Drug Evaluation and Research (CDER). For each drug, three
kinds of review were searched for software names: the integrated, the
multi-discipline and the clinical pharmacology review. Pages that hold only an
image were read by optical character recognition (OCR). Every mention was then
read to decide whose software it was: the sponsor's, the FDA reviewer's, or
neither (for example a citation). The reviews call the sponsor the applicant.
A [tool family](../../docs/glossary.md), meaning a tool with all its versions and
spellings, counts once per drug.

Sometimes the FDA reviewer ran the sponsor's model or dataset in a tool, and
the review names no other tool for the sponsor. That tool then counts as the
sponsor's, as indirect evidence
([revisions](../../sources/fda/results/record_revisions.csv)).

The evidence for the sponsor's software has these grades:

- **Stated:** a document names the sponsor's software.
- **Indirect:** the software is not stated as such, but the review shows it
  was used, for example through a NONMEM control stream in the submitted file
  list or an entry in the abbreviation list. Indirect evidence counts towards
  the shares.
- **Template-only case:** an indirect case whose only evidence is the FDA
  template sentence "The final NONMEM data file for analysis contained ...".
  Reviews have kept this sentence unchanged when the sponsor used another tool,
  so Table 1 gives the shares both with and without these cases.
- **Software not stated:** the review describes a population PK analysis, but
  no document searched names its software.
- **Likely tool:** for a drug whose software is not stated, the single tool
  named in the sponsor's own papers on the drug. It is likely, not verified,
  so the FDA record keeps these drugs as not stated.

The reviews name no software for `r nReviewNotStated` drugs that have a
population PK analysis. For these drugs, two more kinds of document were
searched, and every hit was read: the submission's other review documents, and
the assessment report of the European Medicines Agency (EMA) for the same
active substance
([other documents card](../../sources/fda/other_reviews/README.md)). A tool named
there for the sponsor's population PK analysis counts as stated when the EU
procedure was close in time to the FDA's. It counts as indirect when it comes
from an earlier or later submission, or when the document names the tool only
for a related analysis.

For the drugs whose review names no software, Europe PMC was also searched for
the sponsor's own papers on the drug, by brand name, ingredient or development
code. For a drug still without a named tool, a single tool named in these
papers counts as the likely tool if the papers were published from 4 years
before to 2 years after approval. On the drugs whose review does name the
tool, this rule agreed with the review for
`r sum(valid$inferred == valid$sponsor_tool_family)` of `r nrow(valid)`.
Details are in the [source card](../../sources/fda/SOURCE.md) and the
[cross-check card](../../sources/fda/crosscheck/README.md).

The chart shows each year's approvals by the sponsor's data analysis software.

```{r fda-sponsor, fig.width = 8, fig.height = 4.5, fig.cap = "Stacked bars of CDER novel approvals per year by the sponsor's data analysis software"}
plotFdaSponsor(fda)
```

Of the `r count("Total")` approvals, `r sum(fdaTab$drugs)` name the sponsor's
software, directly or indirectly. Another
`r count("popPK present, software not stated")` describe a population PK
analysis without naming the software, and
`r count("No popPK analysis in review")` contain no population PK analysis.

Table 1 gives the drugs per tool, and each tool's share of the
`r sum(fdaTab$drugs)` drugs with an identifiable tool. It also gives the
shares without the `r nTemplate` template-only cases, and with the likely
tools added (`r sum(withLikely)` drugs).

```{r fda-table}
folded("Table 1. The sponsor's data analysis software", knitr::kable(
  data.frame(
    "Sponsor's data analysis software" = fdaTab$family, Drugs = fdaTab$drugs,
    "Share of the drugs with an identifiable tool" = pct(fdaTab$share),
    "Share excluding template-only cases" = pct(fdaTab$share_excluding_template),
    "Share with the likely tools from the literature added" = pct(as.numeric(withLikely[fdaTab$family]) / sum(withLikely)),
    check.names = FALSE
  ),
  align = "lrrrr"
))
```

Of the `r nReviewNotStated` drugs whose review names no software, the
submission's other documents name it for `r nrow(fdaOther)`. The other
`r nrow(notStated)` are the drugs without a named tool. Table 2 gives the
evidence found in the sponsor's papers for each of them. Only the first row,
a sponsor paper near submission, counts as a likely tool.

```{r fda-crosscheck}
tiers <- c(
  "sponsor paper near submission", "sponsor paper, other years", "sponsor papers name several tools",
  "other authors only", "none"
)
folded("Table 2. Drugs without a named tool: evidence in the sponsor's papers", knitr::kable(
  data.frame(
    "Evidence in the literature" = tiers,
    Drugs = as.integer(table(factor(notStated$evidence, levels = tiers))),
    "Tool named" = vapply(tiers, function(t) {
      x <- table(notStated$inferred[notStated$evidence == t & notStated$inferred != ""])
      if (length(x) == 0) "" else paste(names(x), x, collapse = ", ")
    }, character(1)),
    check.names = FALSE, row.names = NULL
  ),
  align = "lrl"
))
```

**Conclusions**

- Without the template-only cases, NONMEM's share of the drugs with an
  identifiable tool is `r pct(fdaTab$share_excluding_template[1])`.
- The estimation tools searched for that are never the sponsor's tool are
  `r andList(fdaUnused)`.
- The submission's other documents name the tool for `r nrow(fdaOther)` of the
  `r nReviewNotStated` drugs whose review does not. Of these,
  `r sum(fdaOther$evidence_strength == "stated")` are stated and
  `r sum(fdaOther$evidence_strength == "indirect")` indirect.
- The tool these other documents name is always
  `r andList(unique(fdaOther$family))`. All but
  `r sum(fdaOther$source != "EMA assessment report")` of them are EMA
  assessment reports.
- The likely tools from the sponsor's papers are
  `r andList(paste(likelyTab, names(likelyTab)))`.

**Discussion.** The FDA reviews are the only source here that records what
was used in submissions rather than what was mentioned. They trail current
practice, since the analyses are done 1 to 3 years before approval. The main
gap is the drugs for which no document names the software. The cross-check of
the sponsor's papers reaches only `r nrow(likely)` of the `r nrow(notStated)`
drugs. EMA assessment reports agree with the FDA
reviews where both name the tool. They name it for only about a third of the
drugs, so they fill part of the gap rather than make a series of their own.

**By twelve-month period.** Two further charts add a view of the approvals by
July-to-June period, next to the 2021 to 2025 results by calendar year. They do
not replace those results. The periods run from July to June, so that the
latest period ends with the last half-year that is at least three months past.
They cover July 2020 to June 2026. The charts therefore include approvals that
the 2021 to 2025 results do not have: those of July to December 2020 and of
January to June 2026.

*Development run results for the approvals of July to December 2020 and January
to June 2026: read by Claude Code subagents; the numbers may change at the
production run.* For these approvals, the sponsor's software comes from a
[development run](../../docs/glossary.md) of the
[FDA tool use classification](../../classifications/fda_use/card.md), read by
Claude Sonnet 5.5 subagents. When a review names no tool, a
[reading of its own](../../classifications/fda_poppk/card.md) decides between
"software not stated" and "no population PK analysis". These drugs were not
searched in other documents, as the 2021 to 2025 drugs were. The 2021 to 2025
approvals keep their values from the FDA record. "Review not posted" marks one
approval of December 2020 (gallium Ga 68 PSMA-11) for which no review document
was found on Drugs@FDA, the FDA's database of approved drugs. The charts show
the periods as numbers of drugs and as shares.

```{r fda-periods, fig.width = 8, fig.height = 4.5, fig.cap = "Stacked bars of CDER novel approvals per July-to-June period by the sponsor's data analysis software, as numbers of drugs and as shares"}
fdaP <- read.csv("sources/fda/results/fda_periods.csv", colClasses = "character")
plotFdaSponsor(fdaP, by = "period")
plotFdaSponsor(fdaP, by = "period", scale = "percent")
```
## Published literature, 2021 to 2026

*Development run results: read by Claude Code subagents; the numbers may change at the production run.*

**In short.**

- NONMEM is named in `r pct(pmShare[["NONMEM"]])` of the PubMed papers that
  name an estimation tool, and in `r pct(epShare[["NONMEM"]])` of the Europe PMC
  ones. Monolix is named in `r pct(pmShare[["Monolix"]])` and
  `r pct(epShare[["Monolix"]])` of them.
- Phoenix NLME follows with `r pct(pmShare[["Phoenix NLME"]])` (PubMed) and
  `r pct(epShare[["Phoenix NLME"]])` (Europe PMC). Every other tool is at
  `r pct(litRestMax)` or less.
- Counting only the tools the authors used, NONMEM is used in
  `r pct(pmUsed[["NONMEM"]])` (PubMed) and `r pct(epUsed[["NONMEM"]])` (Europe
  PMC) of the papers that use an estimation tool. Monolix is used in
  `r pct(pmUsed[["Monolix"]])` (PubMed) and `r pct(epUsed[["Monolix"]])` (Europe PMC).
- In Europe PMC, `r pct(anyShare[["Europe PMC (full text)"]])` of the papers
  with a model fit of their own name an estimation tool.
- In PubMed, papers with an industry or contract research organisation (CRO)
  first author name NONMEM more often than academic papers:
  `r pct(litAffShare$sponsor[["NONMEM"]])` against
  `r pct(litAffShare$academia[["NONMEM"]])` of the papers naming a tool. The
  industry and CRO group is small, with `r litAffN[["sponsor"]]` papers.

**Methods.** The method has three steps: find the papers, keep those with a
model fit of their own, and count the tools in those. The papers are counted by
publication year, and 2026 is partial. Preprints are left out.

*Finding the papers.* A paper is found by one of two routes, or by both:

- **Term route:** the paper uses the field's names for the method. These are
  "population pharmacokinetic(s)", pharmacometric* (any word that starts so)
  and "(non-)linear mixed effects", which make up the
  [core set](../../docs/glossary.md), retrieved on `r litDate`. They are also the
  short forms such as "population PK", "population pharmacodynamic" and NLME
  (nonlinear mixed effects), which make up the [extension](../../docs/glossary.md).
- **Tool route:** the paper names an [estimation tool](../../docs/glossary.md) made
  for pharmacometric work (NONMEM, Monolix, Phoenix NLME, nlmixr, Pumas,
  Pmetrics, saemix or S-ADAPT), whatever it calls its method.

PubMed is searched in the title and abstract. Europe PMC is searched in the
title, abstract and keywords for the terms. For the tools, it is searched in
the methods of open-access full text.

*Keeping the papers with a model fit of their own.* Every paper found was read
for whether its authors fitted a population model of their own, in pharmacology
(the [relevance classification](../../classifications/lit_relevance/card.md)). Claude
Sonnet 5.5 read the papers. Only papers read as having a model fit of their own
are counted:

- Of the `r sum(litBase$source == "PubMed (title/abstract)")` PubMed papers
  found, `r sum(litBase$source == "PubMed (title/abstract)" & litBase$value == "own_fit")`
  have a model fit of their own.
- Of the `r epBase0` Europe PMC papers found with full text,
  `r sum(litBase$source == "Europe PMC (full text)" & litBase$value == "own_fit")`
  have one.

The papers left out use a published model, are reviews or commentaries, use
mixed-effects models outside pharmacology, or could not be decided. The papers
with a model fit of their own are the row "Papers with a model fit of their
own" in Tables 3 and 4. A blind second reading of a random sample by Claude
Opus 5.5, which did not see the first answers, gave the same value for
`r litRelCheck$agree` of `r litRelCheck$items` papers.

*Counting the tools.* The tools are found in each counted paper's own text,
downloaded once (the [corpus](../../corpus/README.md)). The name patterns are the
same as for PAGE and FDA. In PubMed the text is the title, abstract and
keywords. In Europe PMC it is the full text of the open-access articles,
without the reference list and the back matter. Each tool is counted in two
ways:

- **Naming:** a paper counts for every estimation tool it names.
- **Using:** a paper counts only for the tools its authors used for their own
  analysis, by the [tool use classification](../../classifications/tool_use/card.md).
  Rules decide the clear cases and Claude Sonnet 5.5 reads the rest. A blind
  second reading by Claude Opus 5.5 gave the same value for
  `r toolCheck$agree` of `r toolCheck$compared` pairs of a paper and a tool.

The two counts give two kinds of share, with different denominators. A naming
share is out of the papers that name at least one estimation tool. A using
share is out of the papers that use at least one.

The first author's affiliation is taken from the PubMed record. Rules classify
it as industry, CRO, academia, regulator or vendor. The IDs behind every count
are stored. Details are in the [source card](../../sources/literature/SOURCE.md).

**Naming shares.** The chart of naming shares gives each tool's share of the
papers that name at least one estimation tool, per source and year. In PubMed
these are `r pct(anyShare[["PubMed (title/abstract)"]])` of the papers with a
model fit of their own, since software is rarely named in the abstract. In
Europe PMC they are `r pct(anyShare[["Europe PMC (full text)"]])`.

```{r literature, fig.width = 9, fig.height = 4.8, fig.cap = "Share of pharmacometric papers naming each tool per year, among papers naming any estimation tool, PubMed and Europe PMC"}
plotLiteratureShares(litShares,
  measure = "share", families = estimation, partialNote = paste0("2026 is partial (to ", litDate, ")."), log = FALSE,
  denominator = paste(
    "Share of the papers naming at least one estimation tool, per source and year;",
    "a paper can name several tools, so the shares can add up to more than 100%."
  )
)
```

Tables 3 and 4 give the naming counts per year, including the tools too rare
to see in the chart.

```{r literature-table-pubmed}
folded("Table 3. PubMed (title/abstract): papers per tool and year", countTable(
  litShares[litShares$source == "PubMed (title/abstract)", c("year", "software", "n", "n_any", "base_n")] |>
    setNames(c("year", "family", "n", "n_any", "base_n")), "base_n", "Papers with a model fit of their own"
))
```

```{r literature-table-epmc}
folded("Table 4. Europe PMC (full text): papers per tool and year", countTable(
  litShares[litShares$source == "Europe PMC (full text)", c("year", "software", "n", "n_any", "base_n")] |>
    setNames(c("year", "family", "n", "n_any", "base_n")), "base_n", "Papers with a model fit of their own"
))
```

**Using shares.** The chart of using shares gives each tool's share of the
papers that use at least one estimation tool for their own analysis. These are
`r pct(usedAny[["PubMed (title/abstract)"]])` of the PubMed papers with a model
fit of their own, and `r pct(usedAny[["Europe PMC (full text)"]])` of the
Europe PMC ones.

```{r literature-used, fig.width = 9, fig.height = 4.8, fig.cap = "Share of pharmacometric papers using each tool per year, among papers using any estimation tool, PubMed and Europe PMC"}
plotLiteratureShares(litUsedShares,
  measure = "share", families = estimation, partialNote = "2026 is partial.", log = FALSE,
  title = "Share of pharmacometric papers using each tool",
  denominator = paste(
    "Share of the papers using at least one estimation tool for their own analysis, per source and year,",
    "by the tool use classification; a paper can use several tools."
  )
) + ggplot2::labs(y = "Share of papers using a tool")
```

Table 4b gives, per tool, the number of papers naming it and the number using
it.

```{r literature-used-table}
nu <- merge(
  aggregate(n ~ source + software, litShares, sum), aggregate(n ~ source + software, litUsedShares, sum),
  by = c("source", "software"), all = TRUE, suffixes = c("_named", "_used")
)
nu[is.na(nu)] <- 0
nu <- nu[order(nu$source, -nu$n_named), ]
folded("Table 4b. Papers naming and using each tool, 2021 to 2026", knitr::kable(
  data.frame(Source = nu$source, Tool = nu$software, Naming = nu$n_named, Using = nu$n_used),
  align = "llrr", row.names = FALSE
))
```

**Naming shares by affiliation.** The chart of PubMed naming shares by
affiliation splits the PubMed papers that name a tool by the first author's
affiliation: industry and CRO against academia. Of the
`r sum(anyTool$n_any[anyTool$source == "PubMed (title/abstract)"])` PubMed
papers that name a tool, `r litAffN[["sponsor"]]` have an industry or CRO first
author. `r litAffN[["academia"]]` have an academic one. The others have a first
author from a regulator or a vendor, or no classified affiliation.

```{r literature-affiliation, fig.width = 9, fig.height = 4.5, fig.cap = "Share of PubMed papers naming each tool per year, among papers naming any tool, industry and CRO against academia"}
a <- litAff
names(a)[names(a) == "software"] <- "family"
plotPageShares(a,
  measure = "share", minAbstracts = 10, unit = "papers",
  groupLabels = c(sponsor = "Industry and CRO", academia = "Academia"),
  title = "Share of PubMed papers naming each tool, by first author's affiliation", xlab = NULL,
  caption = paste(
    "Share of the PubMed papers naming at least one estimation tool in the title or abstract, per first author's",
    "affiliation group and year. 2026 is partial."
  )
) + ggplot2::labs(y = "Share of papers naming a tool")
```

Table 5 gives the papers per affiliation group and year.

```{r literature-affiliation-table}
g <- unique(litAff[c("group", "year", "n_any", "base_n")])
folded("Table 5. PubMed papers by first author's affiliation", knitr::kable(
  data.frame(
    " " = c("Industry and CRO: papers", "Industry and CRO: naming a tool", "Academia: papers", "Academia: naming a tool"),
    t(sapply(sort(unique(g$year)), function(y) {
      s <- g[g$year == y & g$group == "sponsor", ]
      a <- g[g$year == y & g$group == "academia", ]
      c(s$base_n, s$n_any, a$base_n, a$n_any)
    })) |> t() |> as.data.frame() |> setNames(sort(unique(g$year))),
    check.names = FALSE
  ),
  align = paste0("l", strrep("r", length(unique(g$year))))
))
```

**Discussion.** The naming series counts mentions. A paper that names a tool
may have used it, compared it or only discussed it. In Europe PMC a tool named
anywhere in the article text counts, the introduction included.

The using series removes comparators and passing mentions. In PubMed it can
only see what the title and abstract say, so a tool named only among the
keywords shows no use.

Every paper was read for a model fit of its own. Reviews, and papers that only
cite a tool, therefore leave both the naming and the using counts.

The tool route was added after a check of the term route alone. That check
showed that the term route held a smaller part of the papers using some tools
(Monolix, Pumas) than of the papers using NONMEM. Papers that name no tool and
do not use the field's names are still missed.

The readers also found a few papers that do name a tool, in a form the search
misses. Examples are NONMEM's expanded name without the word "NONMEM", or a name
that Europe PMC's index does not match. These papers count as naming no tool.

PubMed misses most software, since software is usually named only in the
methods. Both databases keep indexing, so a re-run gives other numbers. The
stored IDs make these numbers reproducible.

## PAGE meeting abstracts, 2016 to 2026

*Development run results: read by Claude Code subagents; the numbers may change at the production run.*

**In short.**

- NONMEM is used in `r pct(pgShare[["NONMEM"]])` of the `r nAny` abstracts
  that use an estimation tool. NONMEM was used in `r pct(pgYear("NONMEM", 2016))` of those
  from 2016 and `r pct(pgYear("NONMEM", 2026))` of those from 2026.
- Monolix is second, with `r pct(pgShare[["Monolix"]])`. Monolix was used in
  `r pct(pgYear("Monolix", 2016))` of those from 2016 and
  `r pct(pgYear("Monolix", 2026))` of those from 2026.
- nlmixr and Stan/Torsten follow, with `r pct(pgShare[["nlmixr"]])` and
  `r pct(pgShare[["Stan/Torsten"]])`. Every other tool is at
  `r pct(pgRestMax)` or less.
- Industry and CRO abstracts and academic abstracts name the tools in similar
  proportions. NONMEM is in `r pct(pgAffShare$sponsor[["NONMEM"]])` of the
  industry and CRO abstracts and `r pct(pgAffShare$academia[["NONMEM"]])` of
  the academic ones. For Monolix the two shares are
  `r pct(pgAffShare$sponsor[["Monolix"]])` and
  `r pct(pgAffShare$academia[["Monolix"]])`.

**Methods.** PAGE is the annual meeting of the Population Approach Group in
Europe.

- **Abstracts:** every abstract of the PAGE meetings `r years[1]` to
  `r years[2]` was retrieved from page-meeting.org. There was no meeting in
  2020.
- **Finding the tools:** tools are searched for in the abstract, with the
  authors and references left out. Where the abstract names no tool, they are
  searched for in the poster or slides PDF, and every hit there was read by
  hand.
- **Use:** the [tool use classification](../../classifications/tool_use/card.md)
  decides what the authors did with each tool the abstract names, as for the
  literature. Rules decide first. Claude Sonnet 5.5 subagents read the rest
  (the [reading](../../docs/glossary.md)), and Claude Opus 5.5 subagents read a
  sample again without seeing those answers (the
  [blind check](../../docs/glossary.md)).
- **What counts:** only the [estimation tools](../../docs/glossary.md) the authors
  used. A tool named as a comparator or in passing does not count.
- **Against the earlier reading:** the earlier reading of the same abstracts
  gives the same value for `r pct(pageOld$share, 1)` of the tools. That is
  `r sum(pageOldTab$Freq[as.character(pageOldTab$old) == as.character(pageOldTab$new)])`
  of the `r sum(pageOldTab$Freq)` pairs of abstract and tool that both readings
  decided.
- **Left out:** the `r nDemo` abstracts of the Software Demonstration session,
  since they are about a tool rather than its use.
- **Affiliation:** the first author's [affiliation type](../../docs/glossary.md)
  (academia, industry, contract research organisation (CRO), software vendor
  or regulator) is decided by rules from the affiliation text, as for the
  literature.

Details are in the [source card](../../sources/page/SOURCE.md).

Of the `r nAbs` abstracts, `r nNamed` name an estimation tool. Of the same
`r nAbs`, `r nAny` (`r pct(nAny / nAbs)`) used one. The chart of tool shares
per meeting year shows each tool's share of those `r nAny` abstracts.

```{r page, fig.width = 9, fig.height = 4.5, fig.cap = "Share of PAGE abstracts using each tool per meeting year, among abstracts using any tool"}
plotPageShares(shares[shares$group == "all", ],
  measure = "share",
  caption = paste(
    "Share of the abstracts using at least one estimation tool, without Software Demonstration abstracts;",
    "a tool counts if the authors used it (a comparator or a passing mention does not), as named in the",
    "abstract or, where the abstract names none, the poster PDF. An abstract can use several tools."
  )
) + ggplot2::theme(strip.text = ggplot2::element_blank())
```

Table 6 gives the using counts per tool and year.

```{r page-table}
folded("Table 6. PAGE abstracts using each tool, per year", countTable(shares[shares$group == "all", ], "n_abstracts", "Abstracts", anyLabel = "Using an estimation tool"))
```

The first authors of the `r sum(affTab)` abstracts outside the Software
Demonstration session have these affiliation types:

- academia: `r affTab[["academia"]]`;
- industry: `r affTab[["industry"]]`;
- CRO: `r affTab[["CRO"]]`;
- software vendor: `r affTab[["vendor"]]`;
- regulator: `r affTab[["regulator"]]`;
- not classified by the rules: `r affTab[["unclassified"]]`.

These counts include the
`r sum(!recent$software_demo & recent$estimation_source == "unknown")`
abstracts whose PDF had to be searched but could not be read. Those abstracts
are left out of the tool shares, which is why the shares count `r nAbs`
abstracts.

The chart by affiliation compares the abstracts with an industry or CRO first
author against those with an academic first author.

```{r page-affiliation, fig.width = 9, fig.height = 4.5, fig.cap = "Share of PAGE abstracts using a tool that use each tool, industry and CRO against academia"}
plotPageShares(shares[shares$group %in% c("sponsor", "academia"), ],
  measure = "share",
  title = "Share of PAGE abstracts using each tool, by first author's affiliation",
  caption = "Share of the abstracts of that affiliation group and year that use any estimation tool."
)
```

Table 7 gives the abstracts per affiliation group and year.

```{r page-affiliation-table}
g <- unique(shares[shares$group %in% c("sponsor", "academia"), c("group", "year", "n_any", "n_abstracts")])
folded("Table 7. PAGE abstracts by first author's affiliation", knitr::kable(
  data.frame(
    " " = c("Industry and CRO: abstracts", "Industry and CRO: using a tool", "Academia: abstracts", "Academia: using a tool"),
    sapply(sort(unique(g$year)), function(y) {
      s <- g[g$year == y & g$group == "sponsor", ]
      a <- g[g$year == y & g$group == "academia", ]
      c(s$n_abstracts, s$n_any, a$n_abstracts, a$n_any)
    }) |> as.data.frame() |> setNames(sort(unique(g$year))),
    check.names = FALSE
  ),
  align = paste0("l", strrep("r", length(unique(g$year))))
))
```

**Discussion.** PAGE is a European meeting, and
`r pct(affTab[["academia"]] / sum(affTab))` of the first authors are academic.
An abstract shows work as of the abstract deadline in March of the meeting
year. PAGE is therefore the most current of the sources, but it is not a
sample of industry work.

The counts are the tools the authors say they used. Abstracts in PAGE's
methodology sessions that develop or test a tool count like any other. The
prediction [From methodology to applied work](#2-from-methodology-to-applied-work)
counts the methodology and applied abstracts separately.

## Analysis types by tool

*Development run results: read by Claude Code subagents (Claude Sonnet 5, 2026-09-27 to 2026-09-29); the numbers may change at the production run.*

**In short.**

- In FDA submissions, the sponsor's estimation tool is used for population
  pharmacokinetics (PK) alone for `r pct(fdaPkOnly)` of the `r nrow(fdaAt)`
  drugs whose review names that tool. At PAGE, `r pct(pagePkOnly)` of the
  `r nrow(pageAt)` abstracts that used a tool are PK only.
- At PAGE, NONMEM carries most of the plain PK work, and the other tools lean
  towards the more complex analyses.
- Stan/Torsten leans towards full Bayesian models. This is expected, since a
  model fitted in Stan is a full Bayesian model.
- nlmixr, Pumas and Stan/Torsten have few abstracts, and most of them are in
  methodology sessions. Their leanings therefore describe methods work more
  than applied work.
- Monolix leans towards machine learning, but most of those abstracts are
  from 2024 to 2026 and in methodology sessions. An earlier Monolix lean
  towards QSP and PBPK did not survive the reading.

**Methods.**

- **Items:** every abstract of the PAGE meetings since 2016 and every PubMed
  and Europe PMC paper that names an [estimation tool](../../docs/glossary.md) is
  classified by analysis type. PAGE is the annual meeting of the Population
  Approach Group in Europe. The type is decided from the title and abstract.
- **Types:** the types run in order of complexity from PK only to
  quantitative systems pharmacology (QSP) and physiologically based
  pharmacokinetic (PBPK) models, as listed in Table 8. PK/PD stands for
  pharmacokinetic-pharmacodynamic, AI for artificial intelligence, and a
  neural ODE is a neural ordinary differential equation. Joint models are
  counted with time-to-event, as they are rare. An item can have several
  types.
- **PAGE:** the abstracts were read for their types together with the tool
  roles in an earlier reading, by Claude Sonnet 5 readers. A
  [blind check](../../docs/glossary.md) gave the same set of types for
  `r rc("same set of types")$both` of the
  `r rc("abstracts compared")$first_reader` abstracts it compared. The tools
  are those that reading found used.
- **Literature:** keyword rules decide the types. A Claude Sonnet 5 reader
  checked a fresh sample against the type definitions and agreed with the
  rules on `r litCheck$agree` of `r litCheck$rows` items.
- **Tools in the literature:** for Europe PMC the tool is the one that fitted
  the final model, as read for the analysis of model and data size
  (`analysis/model_size/`). A tool named only as a comparator therefore does
  not count. In PubMed every tool named counts.
- **FDA reviews:** the keyword rules did not work on these, because a review
  mixes several analyses, tools and template sections on every page; two checks
  of the rules agreed with fewer than half of the drugs. Claude Sonnet 5
  readers read the text around each mention of the sponsor's tool instead. A check of
  the reading agreed for `r fdaCheck$agree` of `r fdaCheck$rows` drugs.
- **Presentation:** PubMed and the FDA reviews have few complex analyses, so
  they are shown only as PK only against any other type.

Details are in the [method card](../../analysis/analysis_types/README.md).

The chart of analysis types per source shows, for each source, the share of
the items with each type.

```{r types-spread, fig.width = 11, fig.height = 4, fig.cap = "Share of items naming an estimation tool with each analysis type, per source"}
plotTypeSpread(spread,
  caption = paste(
    "Share of the items with an estimation tool that have each type (PAGE: abstracts using one; Europe PMC: papers",
    "fitting a model with one; PubMed: papers naming one; FDA: drugs, what the sponsor's tool was used for). An item",
    "can have several types. The number of items is in each panel title."
  )
) + ggplot2::labs(title = "What the tools are used for")
```

Table 8 gives the counts.

```{r types-spread-table}
typeOrder <- c(lumpedTypes, "Any type other than PK only")
tab <- data.frame(Type = typeOrder[typeOrder %in% spread$type])
for (s in unique(spread$source)) {
  tab[[gsub("\n", " ", s)]] <- vapply(tab$Type, function(ty) {
    r <- spread[spread$source == s & spread$type == ty, ]
    if (nrow(r) == 0) "" else sprintf("%d (%s)", r$n, pct(r$share))
  }, "")
}
folded("Table 8. Items with each analysis type, per source", knitr::kable(
  tab,
  align = paste0("l", strrep("r", ncol(tab) - 1))
))
```

The chart of ratios compares the tools at PAGE. For each tool and type, it
divides the tool's share of the type by the share among the abstracts that do
not use the tool. The 95% interval of each ratio is computed on the log scale
(the Katz method). A tool leans towards a type when the whole interval is above
1, and away from it when the whole interval is below 1.

```{r types-lift, fig.width = 10, fig.height = 5.5, fig.cap = "PAGE 2016 to 2026: how much more or less common each type is among a tool's abstracts than among the other tools' abstracts"}
plotTypeLift(lift,
  caption = paste(
    "PAGE abstracts 2016 to 2026 using an estimation tool, without Software Demonstration abstracts. Ratio of the",
    "tool's share of the type to the share among abstracts not using the tool, with 95% intervals; 1 means no",
    "difference. Missing points: no abstract of that tool has the type."
  )
) + ggplot2::labs(title = "Which tools lean towards which analyses (PAGE, 2016 to 2026)")
```

Table 9 gives the ratios, intervals and counts.

```{r types-lift-table}
folded("Table 9. PAGE 2016 to 2026: ratio of each tool's share of a type to the other tools' share", knitr::kable(
  data.frame(
    Tool = lift$tool, Type = lift$type,
    "Abstracts with the type" = sprintf("%d of %d", lift$n, lift$n_tool),
    "Ratio (95% interval)" = ifelse(is.na(lift$ratio), "",
      sprintf("%.1f (%.1f to %.1f)", lift$ratio, lift$lower, lift$upper)
    ),
    check.names = FALSE, row.names = NULL
  ),
  align = "llrr"
))
```

**Conclusions.** The first conclusion comes from Table 8, the leanings of the
tools from Table 9. A tool "leans towards no type" when none of its intervals
lies wholly above 1.

```{r types-conclusions}
knitr::asis_output(paste(c(
  paste0(
    "- In FDA submissions the sponsor's estimation tool is used for population PK alone for ",
    pct(fdaPkOnly), " of the drugs; at PAGE, ", pct(pagePkOnly), " of the abstracts are PK only."
  ),
  vapply(liftTools, toolBullet, "")
), collapse = "\n"))
```

**Discussion.** nlmixr, Pumas and Stan/Torsten have few PAGE abstracts, and
most of them are in methodology sessions (the PAGE sessions on methods,
recognised from the session label). Their leanings therefore describe methods
work more than applied work. For each tool, the number of abstracts that used
it and the share of its abstracts in methodology sessions:

- NONMEM: `r nTool[["NONMEM"]]` abstracts, `r pct(methShare[["NONMEM"]])` in
  methodology sessions;
- Monolix: `r nTool[["Monolix"]]` abstracts,
  `r pct(methShare[["Monolix"]])` in methodology sessions;
- nlmixr: `r nTool[["nlmixr"]]` abstracts, `r pct(methShare[["nlmixr"]])` in
  methodology sessions;
- Pumas: `r nTool[["Pumas"]]` abstracts, `r pct(methShare[["Pumas"]])` in
  methodology sessions;
- Stan/Torsten: `r nTool[["Stan/Torsten"]]` abstracts,
  `r pct(methShare[["Stan/Torsten"]])` in methodology sessions.

The FDA figure covers only what the sponsor's estimation tool was used for.
The reviews also describe analyses done with other tools, and those are not
counted. An example is an exposure-response analysis in R next to a NONMEM
population PK model. In PubMed, every tool named counts, and a mention is not
proof of use.

Two Monolix leanings were checked abstract by abstract, by a reader asked to
test the claim. The
`r liftN("Monolix", "Machine learning, AI, neural ODEs")` machine learning
abstracts are all Monolix-based machine learning work. Most are from 2024 to
2026 and in methodology sessions. Some are vendor tool development, or neural
ODEs implemented in several tools at once.

The earlier lean towards QSP and PBPK did not survive the reading. Of the
`r liftN("Monolix", "QSP, PBPK")` abstracts left, 8 used Monolix for another
part of the work. The PBPK model in those abstracts was built in another tool,
or in a tool not stated. They count as QSP or PBPK for Monolix because each
abstract gets its types as a whole, not per tool.

```{r ms-setup, include = FALSE}
msx <- read.csv("analysis/model_size/extractions.csv", colClasses = "character")
msd <- modelSizeData(msx)
msChecks <- read.csv("analysis/model_size/results/checks.csv")
chk <- function(f) msChecks[msChecks$field == f, ]
nmMx <- msd[msd$tool %in% c("NONMEM", "Monolix"), ]
nmMx <- nmMx[order(nmMx$tool != "NONMEM"), ]
ms1 <- nmMx[nmMx$n_models %in% 1, ] # one final model per paper
msPk <- ms1[ms1$analysis %in% "pk_only", ]
msMeasures <- c("fixed", "random", "structural", "covariates", "iov", "covariances", "residual")
msMean <- function(d, tool, m) {
  s <- modelSizeSummary(d[d$tool == tool, ], measures = m)
  s
}
ratioRows <- function(d, label, tools) {
  do.call(rbind, lapply(c("fixed", "random", "structural", "covariates"), function(m) {
    do.call(rbind, lapply(c(FALSE, TRUE), function(a) cbind(comparison = label, modelSizeRatio(d, m, adjust = a, tools = tools))))
  }))
}
alg <- msd[msd$n_models %in% 1 & msd$algorithm %in% c("FOCE", "SAEM"), ]
alg$tool_orig <- alg$tool
alg$tool <- alg$algorithm
msRatios <- rbind(
  ratioRows(ms1, "Monolix against NONMEM, all models", c("NONMEM", "Monolix")),
  ratioRows(msPk, "Monolix against NONMEM, PK only", c("NONMEM", "Monolix")),
  ratioRows(alg, "SAEM against FOCE (any tool), all models", c("FOCE", "SAEM"))
)
rr <- function(comparison, m, adjusted = TRUE) msRatios[msRatios$comparison == comparison & msRatios$measure == m & msRatios$adjusted == adjusted, ]
fmtRatio <- function(r) sprintf("%.2f (%.2f to %.2f)", r$ratio, r$lower, r$upper)
direction <- function(r, what) {
  if (r$upper < 1) paste("fewer", what, "than") else if (r$lower > 1) paste("more", what, "than") else paste("about as many", what, "as")
}
sm <- function(d, tool, m) {
  x <- d[[m]][d$tool == tool]
  mean(x, na.rm = TRUE)
}
summedAdj <- rbind(modelSizeRatio(nmMx, "fixed", TRUE), modelSizeRatio(nmMx, "random", TRUE))
dsTools <- names(sort(table(msd$tool[!is.na(msd$n_subjects)]), decreasing = TRUE))
dsTools <- dsTools[table(msd$tool[!is.na(msd$n_subjects)])[dsTools] >= 10]
medSubj <- vapply(dsTools, function(t) stats::median(msd$n_subjects[msd$tool == t], na.rm = TRUE), numeric(1))
nAlgStated <- sum(nmMx$tool == "NONMEM" & !nmMx$algorithm %in% "Not stated")
```
## Model and data size by tool

*Development run results: read by Claude Code subagents; the numbers may change at the production run.*

**In short.**

- The hypothesis that the SAEM method (stochastic approximation expectation
  maximisation, the Monolix default) leads to larger models holds for the
  random effects, but not for the fixed effects. Models fitted with Monolix,
  and with SAEM whatever the tool, carry more terms for inter-individual
  variability (IIV). NONMEM models carry more covariate effects before
  adjustment, but not after: the adjusted ratio for the covariate effects is
  `r fmtRatio(rr("Monolix against NONMEM, all models", "covariates"))`.
- Monolix models have `r direction(rr("Monolix against NONMEM, all models", "random"), "random effects")`
  NONMEM models: `r sprintf("%.1f", sm(ms1, "Monolix", "random"))`
  against `r sprintf("%.1f", sm(ms1, "NONMEM", "random"))` IIV terms on average.
  The adjusted ratio is `r fmtRatio(rr("Monolix against NONMEM, all models", "random"))`.
  For models of the pharmacokinetics alone (PK only) it is
  `r fmtRatio(rr("Monolix against NONMEM, PK only", "random"))`.
- Before adjustment, Monolix models have `r direction(rr("Monolix against NONMEM, all models", "fixed", FALSE), "fixed effects")`
  NONMEM models: `r sprintf("%.1f", sm(ms1, "Monolix", "fixed"))`
  against `r sprintf("%.1f", sm(ms1, "NONMEM", "fixed"))` on average. The
  difference lies mainly in the covariate effects:
  `r sprintf("%.1f", sm(ms1, "Monolix", "covariates"))` against
  `r sprintf("%.1f", sm(ms1, "NONMEM", "covariates"))`.
- Adjusted for analysis type, data size and year, the fixed-effect ratio is
  `r fmtRatio(rr("Monolix against NONMEM, all models", "fixed"))`. For PK only
  models it is `r fmtRatio(rr("Monolix against NONMEM, PK only", "fixed"))`.
- By estimation method, SAEM models have `r direction(rr("SAEM against FOCE (any tool), all models", "random"), "random effects")`
  models fitted by first-order conditional estimation
  (FOCE), with an adjusted ratio of
  `r fmtRatio(rr("SAEM against FOCE (any tool), all models", "random"))`. They
  have `r direction(rr("SAEM against FOCE (any tool), all models", "fixed"), "fixed effects")`
  FOCE models, with a ratio of
  `r fmtRatio(rr("SAEM against FOCE (any tool), all models", "fixed"))`.

**Methods.** The hypothesis is that SAEM, the Monolix default, is more
permissive than NONMEM's gradient-based methods, and so leads to larger
models. The terms used here:

- **Fixed effects:** the structural fixed effects plus the covariate effects
  of the final model. Residual error parameters are not counted.
- **Random effects:** the inter-individual variability (IIV) terms of the
  final model.
- **IOV:** inter-occasion variability.
- **SAEM:** stochastic approximation expectation maximisation, the default
  estimation method of Monolix.
- **FOCE:** first-order conditional estimation, a gradient-based method of
  NONMEM.
- **PK only:** a model of the pharmacokinetics (PK) alone.

The papers are those of the Europe PMC [core set](../../docs/glossary.md) from 2021
to 2026 that name an estimation tool: `r nrow(msx)` papers. Claude Sonnet 5
read each paper and recorded:

- whether the authors fitted a population model of their own;
- the fitting tool, the estimation method and the analysis type;
- from the final parameter table, the number of structural fixed effects,
  covariate effects, IIV terms, IOV terms, random-effect covariances and
  residual error parameters;
- the number of subjects and of observations in the data.

A blind check by Claude Opus 5.5 read a random `r chk("own_fit")$sample` of the
`r nrow(msx)` papers again. The two readers agreed on the tool for
`r chk("tool")$agree_exact` of `r chk("tool")$compared` papers. They agreed on
the fixed effects for `r chk("fixed effects")$agree_exact` of
`r chk("fixed effects")$compared` papers, and on the random effects for
`r chk("random effects (IIV)")$agree_exact` of `r chk("random effects (IIV)")$compared`.
Their counts showed no systematic difference.

The tool comparison uses the papers with a single final model, since several
models added together would read as one large model. Of these,
`r sum(ms1$tool == "NONMEM" & !is.na(ms1$fixed))` NONMEM papers and
`r sum(ms1$tool == "Monolix" & !is.na(ms1$fixed))` Monolix papers give a count
of their fixed effects. Not every paper gives every part of the model, so the
number of papers differs a little from part to part; Table 10 gives it for
each. The ratio of the Monolix mean to the NONMEM mean comes from a
quasi-Poisson regression of the count on the tool. It is given crude, and
adjusted for analysis type, data size (the log number of subjects) and
publication year. The same regression compares SAEM with FOCE, whatever the
tool. Details: [method card](../../analysis/model_size/README.md).

The model-size chart shows the distribution of fixed and random effects in the
final models, with the mean and its 95% interval, for all models and for PK
only models.

```{r model-size, fig.width = 8, fig.height = 5.5, fig.cap = "Fixed and random effects in the final model, NONMEM against Monolix, all models and PK only"}
plotModelSize(ms1,
  caption = paste(
    "Europe PMC papers 2021 to 2026 whose authors fitted one final population model with NONMEM or Monolix.",
    "Fixed effects: structural plus covariate effects; random effects: IIV terms.",
    "Violins: the distribution of counts; points and bars: the mean and its 95% interval."
  )
) + ggplot2::labs(title = "Model size: NONMEM against Monolix")
```

Table 10 gives the mean of every part of the final model, per tool.

```{r model-size-table}
cellMean <- function(d, tool, m) {
  s <- modelSizeSummary(d[d$tool == tool, ], measures = m)
  if (nrow(s) == 0 || s$n == 0) "" else sprintf("%.1f (%.1f to %.1f), n=%d", s$mean, s$lower, s$upper, s$n)
}
msLabels <- c(
  fixed = "Fixed effects (structural + covariate)", random = "Random effects (IIV)", structural = "Structural fixed effects",
  covariates = "Covariate effects", iov = "IOV terms", covariances = "Random-effect covariances", residual = "Residual error parameters"
)
folded("Table 10. Mean number of parameters in the final model (95% interval, papers)", knitr::kable(
  data.frame(
    Parameters = unname(msLabels[msMeasures]),
    "NONMEM, all" = vapply(msMeasures, function(m) cellMean(ms1, "NONMEM", m), ""),
    "Monolix, all" = vapply(msMeasures, function(m) cellMean(ms1, "Monolix", m), ""),
    "NONMEM, PK only" = vapply(msMeasures, function(m) cellMean(msPk, "NONMEM", m), ""),
    "Monolix, PK only" = vapply(msMeasures, function(m) cellMean(msPk, "Monolix", m), ""),
    check.names = FALSE, row.names = NULL
  ),
  align = "lrrrr"
))
```

Table 11 gives the ratio of Monolix to NONMEM means, crude and adjusted, and
the same ratio for SAEM against FOCE whatever the tool.

```{r model-size-ratios}
wide <- do.call(rbind, lapply(split(msRatios, list(msRatios$comparison, msRatios$measure), drop = TRUE), function(x) {
  data.frame(
    Comparison = x$comparison[1], Parameters = unname(msLabels[x$measure[1]]),
    "Crude ratio (95% interval)" = fmtRatio(x[!x$adjusted, ]), "Adjusted ratio (95% interval)" = fmtRatio(x[x$adjusted, ]),
    "Papers (adjusted)" = x$n[x$adjusted], check.names = FALSE
  )
}))
wide <- wide[order(match(wide$Comparison, unique(msRatios$comparison)), match(wide$Parameters, msLabels)), ]
folded("Table 11. Ratio of mean parameter counts, crude and adjusted for analysis type, data size and year", knitr::kable(
  wide,
  row.names = FALSE, align = "llrrr"
))
```

The data-size chart shows the number of subjects and of observations in the
dataset of the final model, per tool.

```{r data-size, fig.width = 9, fig.height = 6, fig.cap = "Subjects and observations in the dataset of the final model, per tool"}
plotDataSize(msd,
  minPapers = 10,
  caption = paste(
    "Europe PMC papers 2021 to 2026 whose authors fitted a population model of their own, per fitting tool with at least",
    "10 papers giving the number of subjects. Log scale; the point marks the median; n = papers."
  )
) + ggplot2::labs(title = "Data size per tool")
```

Table 12 gives the medians and quartiles of the data size, per tool.

```{r data-size-table}
q <- function(x) {
  x <- x[!is.na(x)]
  if (!length(x)) "" else sprintf("%s (%s to %s)", format(round(stats::median(x)), big.mark = ","),
    format(round(stats::quantile(x, 0.25)), big.mark = ","), format(round(stats::quantile(x, 0.75)), big.mark = ","))
}
folded("Table 12. Data size per tool: median (quartiles) and papers", knitr::kable(
  data.frame(
    Tool = dsTools,
    "Papers, own fit" = vapply(dsTools, function(t) sum(msd$tool == t), numeric(1)),
    "Subjects" = vapply(dsTools, function(t) q(msd$n_subjects[msd$tool == t]), ""),
    "Papers giving subjects" = vapply(dsTools, function(t) sum(!is.na(msd$n_subjects[msd$tool == t])), numeric(1)),
    "Observations" = vapply(dsTools, function(t) q(msd$n_obs[msd$tool == t]), ""),
    "Papers giving observations" = vapply(dsTools, function(t) sum(!is.na(msd$n_obs[msd$tool == t])), numeric(1)),
    check.names = FALSE, row.names = NULL
  ),
  align = "lrrrrr"
```
