
**Conclusions**

- The median dataset has `r andList(paste(round(medSubj), "subjects for", names(medSubj)))`.

**Discussion.** Most of the fixed-effect difference between the tools goes
with data size and analysis type. The adjusted ratio is close to 1
overall`r if (rr("Monolix against NONMEM, PK only", "fixed")$upper < 1) paste0(", although PK only models keep a small difference, ", fmtRatio(rr("Monolix against NONMEM, PK only", "fixed"))) else ""`.

SAEM models are mostly Monolix models: `r sum(alg$algorithm == "SAEM" & alg$tool_orig == "Monolix")`
of `r sum(alg$algorithm == "SAEM")`. The comparison by estimation method
therefore adds little to the comparison by tool. The papers cannot tell
whether the extra random effects come from the estimation method or from how
models are usually built in each tool.

The NONMEM papers state the estimation method in `r nAlgStated` of
`r sum(nmMx$tool == "NONMEM")` cases. The counts come only from papers that
show the final estimates in the article text.

Counting all final models of a paper together gives an adjusted ratio of
`r fmtRatio(summedAdj[1, ])` for the fixed effects. For the random effects it
is `r fmtRatio(summedAdj[2, ])`.

The data are observational: tool, data and purpose come together. The
adjustment removes only what analysis type, data size and year explain.

## Predictions

*Development run results: read by Claude Code subagents; the numbers may change at the production run.*

Two ways of reading ahead from the data: how far regulatory submissions trail
what industry shows at PAGE, and how methodology work at PAGE turns into
applied work some years later.

### 1. The lag of FDA submissions behind PAGE

**In short.**

- NONMEM's share of the PAGE abstracts from industry and contract research
  organisations (CROs) follows a trend from `r pct(pageLevel[1])` in 2016 to
  `r pct(pageLevel[2])` in 2026.
- NONMEM's share of the FDA approvals of 2021 to 2025 is `r pct(fdaLevel)`.
  That is `r sum(fdaNm$n)` of the `r sum(fdaNm$n_any)` drugs with an
  identifiable tool.
- Extended back in time, the PAGE trend reaches NONMEM's FDA share only around
  `r round(crossYear)`. That year lies before the PAGE data begin, so it says
  only that the FDA series trails PAGE by more than a decade.
- Lags of `r min(plausible)` to `r max(plausible)` years fit about as well
  (relative likelihood above 0.15)`r if (atEdge) paste0(", and the best fit is at ", best, " years, the longest lag the PAGE years allow. The lag is therefore a lower bound, not an estimate") else ""`.

**Methods.** The idea is that PAGE shows what industry does now, while FDA
reviews show analyses done years earlier. If so, the FDA share of a tool in approval year t should
equal the PAGE share in year t minus some lag. The PAGE share is taken among
the abstracts that used a tool and whose first author works in industry or at
a CRO. The FDA share is taken among the drugs with an identifiable tool: those
whose review states, directly or indirectly, the tool the applicant used.

The test uses NONMEM, the only tool with enough FDA counts. A logistic trend
in year is fitted to NONMEM's PAGE share from `r pageYears[1]` to
`r pageYears[2]`. Each lag from `r min(lags)` to `r max(lags)` years is then
scored by its binomial likelihood. This is the probability of the yearly FDA
counts if the FDA share in each year were the PAGE trend that many years
earlier. The relative likelihood of a lag is its likelihood divided by that of
the best-fitting lag, so the best lag has a relative likelihood of 1. A lag
with a relative likelihood near 0 fits the FDA counts far worse than the best
lag.

The lag chart shows how well each lag fits the FDA counts, relative to the
best-fitting lag.

```{r lag-profile, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 3.5, fig.cap = "Relative likelihood of each lag between the PAGE trend and FDA approvals"}
plotLagProfile(profile) + ggplot2::labs(title = "How well each lag fits the FDA counts (NONMEM)")
```

Table 13 gives the relative likelihood of each lag.

```{r lag-profile-table}
folded("Table 13. Relative likelihood of each lag", knitr::kable(
  data.frame(
    "Lag (years)" = profile$lag, "Relative likelihood" = formatC(profile$rel_lik, format = "f", digits = 2),
    check.names = FALSE
  ),
  align = "rr"
))
```

The projection chart shows the yearly NONMEM shares at PAGE and at FDA, the
PAGE trend, and the FDA share projected from the trend at the best-fitting
lag.

```{r lag-projection, fig.width = 8, fig.height = 4.2, fig.cap = "NONMEM share: PAGE industry and CRO abstracts, FDA approvals and the FDA share projected from PAGE"}
plotProjection(pageNm, trend, fdaNm, lag = best, years = 2021:(2026 + best)) +
  ggplot2::labs(
    title = paste0("NONMEM share, with the FDA projected at a ", best, "-year lag"),
    subtitle = "Projection = the PAGE trend moved forward by the lag",
    caption = paste(
      "Shares are of the drugs with an identifiable tool (FDA) and of the industry and CRO abstracts using a tool",
      "(PAGE). Points: yearly shares (FDA with 95% intervals). Line: PAGE trend. Band: projection."
    )
  )
```

Table 14 gives the yearly NONMEM shares at PAGE and at FDA.

```{r lag-table}
yrs <- sort(unique(c(pageNm$year, fdaNm$year)))
cell <- function(d, y) {
  r <- d[d$year == y, ]
  if (nrow(r) == 0) "" else sprintf("%d of %d (%s)", r$n, r$n_any, pct(r$n / r$n_any))
}
folded("Table 14. NONMEM share per year, PAGE industry and CRO abstracts and FDA approvals", knitr::kable(
  data.frame(
    Year = yrs,
    "PAGE, industry and CRO: NONMEM among abstracts using a tool" = vapply(yrs, function(y) cell(pageNm, y), ""),
    "FDA approvals: NONMEM among drugs with an identifiable tool" = vapply(yrs, function(y) cell(fdaNm, y), ""),
    check.names = FALSE
  ),
  align = "lrr"
))
```

**Conclusions**

- `r if (atEdge) paste0("Since ", best, " years is only a lower bound on the lag, the projected shares show what the PAGE trend gives at that lag, not a forecast. ") else ""`At
  the best-fitting lag, the projected NONMEM share of FDA approvals is
  `r pct(projected$share[1])` in 2030 (95% interval `r pct(projected$lower[1])`
  to `r pct(projected$upper[1])`). In `r 2026 + best` it is
  `r pct(projected$share[2])` (95% interval `r pct(projected$lower[2])` to
  `r pct(projected$upper[2])`). The intervals cover only the uncertainty of
  the PAGE trend at that lag, not the uncertainty of the lag itself.

**Discussion.** A lag that long is more than the 1 to 3 years between an
analysis and approval. It would mean one of two things. The tools used in
submissions may change far more slowly than the tools shown at PAGE. Or
submissions may differ from PAGE work in level, which this model cannot tell
apart from a delay: it assumes that the FDA share equals the lagged PAGE share
with no other difference. The analysis is exploratory, and a shorter lag
within the plausible range would bring the projected decline forward.

### 2. From methodology to applied work

**In short.**

- Monolix and BUGS started in methodology sessions and moved into applied
  work within a few years. BUGS has since disappeared from PAGE.
- nlmixr's applied abstracts have grown since 2023, although methodology
  sessions still hold most of them.
- Pumas, and machine learning as a kind of analysis, are still mostly in
  methodology sessions, as Monolix was around 2008.
- Stan/Torsten shows no such shift: it has stayed about evenly split since it
  first appeared.

**Methods.** New tools and new kinds of analysis tend to appear first in
PAGE's methodology sessions, and a few years later in applied work. If so, a
tool that is mostly seen in methodology sessions today is a candidate for
wider applied use tomorrow.

Each PAGE abstract that used a tool is counted as methodology or applied work
by its session. PAGE has titled its methodology sessions with a "Methodology"
prefix since 2014. In 2011 to 2013 it titled them by topic alone, for example
"Estimation methods" or "Model evaluation", so those topics are recognised as
methodology too. Sessions on physiologically based pharmacokinetic (PBPK)
models count as applied work throughout. Machine learning is counted in the
same way, as a kind of analysis in any tool: machine learning, artificial
intelligence (AI) or neural ordinary differential equations (neural ODEs).

The chart counts, for each meeting year, the abstracts using each tool in
methodology and in applied sessions.

```{r methods-applied, fig.width = 10, fig.height = 5.5, fig.cap = "PAGE abstracts per year using each tool, in methodology and in applied sessions"}
plotMethodsApplied(maPlot,
  caption = paste(
    "Abstracts using the tool (or, for machine learning, of that analysis type), without Software Demonstration",
    "abstracts. Methodology sessions recognised by topic, as PAGE labelled them without a Methodology prefix in",
    "2011 to 2013; PBPK sessions count as applied. Each panel has its own scale."
  )
) + ggplot2::labs(title = "PAGE abstracts in methodology and in applied sessions")
```

Table 15 gives each tool's share of abstracts in methodology sessions at two
times. The first is the first four meeting years with at least one abstract
using the tool; the second is 2023 to 2026.

```{r methods-table}
grp <- names(ms)
folded("Table 15. Share of each tool's PAGE abstracts in methodology sessions", knitr::kable(
  data.frame(
    "Tool or type" = grp,
    "First four meeting years" = vapply(grp, function(g) sprintf("%d to %d", ms[[g]]$firstYears[1], ms[[g]]$firstYears[2]), ""),
    "Abstracts, first four years" = vapply(grp, function(g) ms[[g]]$nFirst, numeric(1)),
    "In methodology sessions, first four years" = pct(vapply(grp, function(g) ms[[g]]$first, numeric(1))),
    "Abstracts, 2023 to 2026" = vapply(grp, function(g) ms[[g]]$nLast, numeric(1)),
    "In methodology sessions, 2023 to 2026" = vapply(grp, function(g) if (ms[[g]]$nLast == 0) "" else pct(ms[[g]]$last), ""),
    check.names = FALSE, row.names = NULL
  ),
  align = "llrrrr"
))
```

**Discussion.** If the pattern holds, the applied use of Pumas and of machine
learning should grow over the next few years. But the counts are small, often
under ten abstracts a year. The pattern rests on two tools that have completed the
move and one that is making it. It is suggestive, not a
fitted model. Methodology abstracts about a tool itself are counted like any
other.

```{r aiml-setup, include = FALSE}
aiTerms <- readAiMlTerms("taxonomy/ai_ml_terms.csv")
aiItems <- read.csv("analysis/ai_ml/results/items.csv", colClasses = c(id = "character"))
aiShares <- read.csv("analysis/ai_ml/results/shares.csv")
aiBase <- read.csv("analysis/ai_ml/results/base.csv")
aiFirst <- read.csv("analysis/ai_ml/results/first_by_group.csv", colClasses = "character")
aiTerm <- read.csv("analysis/ai_ml/results/first_by_term.csv", colClasses = "character")
aiChecks <- read.csv("analysis/ai_ml/results/checks.csv")
aiDec <- read.csv("analysis/ai_ml/decisions.csv", colClasses = "character")
aiSources <- c("PAGE", "PubMed", "Europe PMC")
aiLink <- function(source, id) {
  url <- aiItems$url[match(paste(source, id), paste(aiItems$source, aiItems$id))]
  label <- switch(source, PAGE = paste("PAGE abstract", id), PubMed = paste("PMID", id), "Europe PMC" = sub("^MED:", "PMID ", id), FDA = paste("NDA/BLA", id))
  sprintf("[%s](%s)", label, url)
}
aiNote <- function(source, id, group) {
  d <- aiDec[aiDec$source == source & aiDec$id == id & aiDec$decision != "not", ]
  d <- d[aiTerms$group[match(d$term, aiTerms$term)] == group, ]
  d$note[order(d$decision != "used")][1]
}
fy <- function(source, group, what = "first_mentioned") as.integer(aiFirst[[what]][aiFirst$source == source & aiFirst$group == group])
ty <- function(source, term, what = "first_used") {
  x <- aiTerm[[what]][aiTerm$source == source & aiTerm$term == term]
  if (length(x) == 0 || is.na(x)) NA_integer_ else as.integer(x)
}
aiShare <- function(source, group, years, what = "mentioned") {
  d <- aiShares[aiShares$source == source & aiShares$group == group & aiShares$year %in% years, ]
  sum(d[[what]]) / sum(d$base_n)
}
aiTotal <- function(source, group, what = "mentioned") sum(aiShares[[what]][aiShares$source == source & aiShares$group == group])
nPageAll <- sum(aiBase$n[aiBase$source == "PAGE"])
nPageEarly <- sum(aiBase$n[aiBase$source == "PAGE" & aiBase$year < 2006])
aiNItems <- nrow(unique(aiItems[c("source", "id")]))
chkAll <- aiChecks[1, ]
chkCount <- aiChecks[2, ]
fdaAi <- aiItems[aiItems$source == "FDA" & aiItems$decision != "not", ]
aiRun <- readLines("analysis/ai_ml/results/run_info.txt")
epBackOnly <- as.integer(sub(".*Europe PMC (\\d+).*", "\\1", grep("^Server matches", aiRun, value = TRUE)))
aiEarlyMax <- max(aiShares$mentioned[aiShares$source %in% aiSources & aiShares$year < 2016])
```

## AI and machine learning

*Development run results: read by Claude Code subagents; the numbers may change at the production run.*

**In short.**

- Machine learning reached pharmacometrics as neural networks. It was first
  used at PAGE in `r fy("PAGE", "ML")`, in a neural network that predicted the
  pharmacokinetics (PK) and pharmacodynamics (PD) of carboplatin and melphalan
  and was compared with NONMEM. It was first used in PubMed in
  `r fy("PubMed", "ML")`. Until 2015 it appeared in at most `r aiEarlyMax`
  abstracts or papers a year in any source.
- The current wave starts in the late 2010s at PAGE. Random forests were
  first used there in `r ty("PAGE", "random forests")`. Gradient boosting
  followed in `r ty("PAGE", "gradient boosting")`, and neural ordinary
  differential equations (neural ODEs) in `r ty("PAGE", "neural ODEs")`.
- A second wave follows with large language models and AI agents. Large
  language models were first used in PubMed in
  `r ty("PubMed", "large language models")` and at PAGE in
  `r ty("PAGE", "large language models")`. AI agents were first used at PAGE in
  `r ty("PAGE", "AI agents")` and in PubMed in `r ty("PubMed", "AI agents")`.
- Machine learning is mostly used where it is named. It was used in
  `r aiTotal("PubMed", "ML", "used")` of the `r aiTotal("PubMed", "ML")` PubMed
  papers that name it. It was used in `r aiTotal("PAGE", "ML", "used")` of the
  `r aiTotal("PAGE", "ML")` PAGE abstracts that name it. AI is more often a
  word in the background: it was used in `r aiTotal("PubMed", "AI", "used")` of
  the `r aiTotal("PubMed", "AI")` PubMed papers that name it.
- No FDA review of the 2021 to 2025 approvals describes a pharmacometric
  analysis with machine learning or AI.

**Methods.** Two groups of terms are searched in every source
([term list](../../taxonomy/ai_ml_terms.csv)):

- **Machine learning:** the named learning methods, which are
  `r andList(aiTerms$term[aiTerms$group == "ML"])`.
- **AI:** the label and its newer forms, which are
  `r andList(aiTerms$term[aiTerms$group == "AI"])`.

Each source is counted against its own base set, the items of the source in a
year. The sources, and the text searched in each, are:

- **PAGE** (the annual meeting of the Population Approach Group in Europe):
  every abstract of the meetings 1992 to 2026, title and body. That is
  `r nPageAll` abstracts. The `r nPageEarly` abstracts from before 2006 were
  fetched for this analysis only.
- **PubMed:** every paper found by the search terms of the
  [core set](../../docs/glossary.md), from the first such paper in
  `r min(aiBase$year[aiBase$source == "PubMed"])`. The title and abstract are
  searched.
- **Europe PMC:** every paper with open-access full text found by the same
  search terms. The title, abstract, keywords and body are searched, but not
  the reference list or the declarations.
- **FDA:** the reviews of the drugs approved in 2021 to 2025.

In all, `r aiNItems` items name at least one term. In a
[reading](../../docs/glossary.md), Claude Sonnet 5.5 decided for each item and each
term it names whether the term was:

- **Used:** the authors apply or develop the method.
- **Mentioned:** the term appears as background, in a citation, in a review or
  in a proposal.
- **Not the method:** the letters mean something else, such as AI for
  aromatase inhibitor, autoinjector or accumulation index, or the term is only
  in a reference list entry or the name of a funding programme.

The AI label counts as used only when the authors call their own method or
tool AI.

A [blind check](../../docs/glossary.md) by Claude Opus 5.5 read a random
`r chkAll$items` of the items again. Together they hold `r chkAll$rows` item
and term pairs. The two readers gave the same decision
for `r chkAll$agree` of the `r chkAll$rows` pairs. They agreed on whether the
term counts at all (used or mentioned, against not the method) for
`r chkCount$agree` of the `r chkAll$rows` pairs. Claude Opus 5.5 decided the
disagreements. Every item on which a first year in Table 16 or Table 17 rests
was read again in full. Details: [method card](../../analysis/ai_ml/README.md).

The chart of shares per year shows, for each source and year, the share of the
base set that mentions or uses each group.

```{r aiml-shares, fig.width = 9, fig.height = 7, fig.cap = "Share of each source's base set mentioning and using machine learning and AI per year"}
aiPlot <- aiShares[aiShares$source %in% aiSources & aiShares$year >= 1990, ]
plotAiMlShares(aiPlot[order(match(aiPlot$source, aiSources), aiPlot$group, aiPlot$year), ],
  caption = paste(
    "Solid: items naming a term of the group, read as used or mentioned; dashed: read as used. PAGE: all abstracts",
    "of the meeting; PubMed: base set, title and abstract; Europe PMC: base set, open-access full text. 2026 is",
    "partial; no PAGE meeting in 2020. The peaks before 2010 are single items in small base sets (Table 18). Each",
    "panel has its own scale."
  )
) + ggplot2::labs(title = "Machine learning and AI in pharmacometric abstracts and papers")
```

The chart of use in the last ten years narrows this to use alone, with the
three sources together.

```{r aiml-used, fig.width = 9, fig.height = 4.2, fig.cap = "Share of each source's base set using machine learning and AI, the last ten years"}
aiRecent <- max(aiShares$year) - 9:0
plotAiMlUsed(aiShares[aiShares$source %in% aiSources, ], years = aiRecent,
  caption = paste(
    "Items read as using a term of the group (the authors apply or develop the method), as a share of the source's",
    "base set. No PAGE meeting in 2020; 2026 is partial."
  )
) + ggplot2::labs(title = sprintf("Use of machine learning and AI, %d to %d", min(aiRecent), max(aiRecent)))
```

Table 16 gives the first mention and the first use per source. Table 17 gives
the first year per term. Table 18 gives the counts per year; PAGE held no
meeting in 2020, so its cells for that year are empty.

```{r aiml-first}
firstRow <- function(src, g) {
  ym <- fy(src, g)
  yu <- fy(src, g, "first_used")
  idm <- strsplit(aiFirst$ids_mentioned[aiFirst$source == src & aiFirst$group == g], "; ")[[1]]
  idu <- strsplit(aiFirst$ids_used[aiFirst$source == src & aiFirst$group == g], "; ")[[1]]
  data.frame(
    Source = src, Group = if (g == "ML") "Machine learning" else "AI",
    "First mentioned" = ym, "Item" = paste(vapply(idm, function(i) aiLink(src, i), ""), collapse = ", "),
    "First used" = if (is.na(yu)) "" else as.character(yu),
    "Item used" = if (is.na(yu)) "" else paste(vapply(idu, function(i) aiLink(src, i), ""), collapse = ", "),
    "What it was (first use)" = if (is.na(yu)) "" else aiNote(src, idu[1], g),
    check.names = FALSE
  )
}
tab16 <- do.call(rbind, lapply(c(aiSources, "FDA"), function(src) do.call(rbind, lapply(c("ML", "AI"), function(g) firstRow(src, g)))))
folded("Table 16. First mention and first use of machine learning and AI, per source", knitr::kable(tab16, row.names = FALSE))
```

```{r aiml-terms}
termCell <- function(src, term) {
  u <- ty(src, term)
  m <- ty(src, term, "first_mentioned")
  if (is.na(m)) "" else if (is.na(u)) sprintf("(%d)", m) else if (u == m) as.character(u) else sprintf("%d (%d)", u, m)
}
termOrder <- aiTerms$term[order(aiTerms$group != "ML", vapply(aiTerms$term, function(t) min(c(ty("PAGE", t), ty("PubMed", t), ty("Europe PMC", t), 9999), na.rm = TRUE), numeric(1)))]
tab17 <- data.frame(
  Term = termOrder, Group = ifelse(aiTerms$group[match(termOrder, aiTerms$term)] == "ML", "Machine learning", "AI"),
  PAGE = vapply(termOrder, function(t) termCell("PAGE", t), ""),
  PubMed = vapply(termOrder, function(t) termCell("PubMed", t), ""),
  "Europe PMC" = vapply(termOrder, function(t) termCell("Europe PMC", t), ""),
  check.names = FALSE, row.names = NULL
)
folded("Table 17. First year each term was used, and in brackets first mentioned where earlier", knitr::kable(tab17, align = "llrrr"))
```

```{r aiml-counts}
cnt <- function(src, g, y) {
  d <- aiShares[aiShares$source == src & aiShares$group == g & aiShares$year == y, ]
  if (nrow(d) == 0) "" else if (d$mentioned == 0) "0" else sprintf("%d (%d)", d$mentioned, d$used)
}
yrs <- sort(unique(aiShares$year[aiShares$source %in% aiSources & aiShares$mentioned > 0]))
yrs <- min(yrs):max(yrs)
yrs <- yrs[yrs %in% aiShares$year[aiShares$source %in% aiSources]]
baseOf <- function(src, y) {
  n <- aiBase$n[aiBase$source == src & aiBase$year == y]
  if (length(n) == 0) "" else as.character(n)
}
tab18 <- data.frame(
  Year = yrs,
  "PAGE abstracts" = vapply(yrs, function(y) baseOf("PAGE", y), ""),
  "PAGE: ML" = vapply(yrs, function(y) cnt("PAGE", "ML", y), ""), "PAGE: AI" = vapply(yrs, function(y) cnt("PAGE", "AI", y), ""),
  "PubMed papers" = vapply(yrs, function(y) baseOf("PubMed", y), ""),
  "PubMed: ML" = vapply(yrs, function(y) cnt("PubMed", "ML", y), ""), "PubMed: AI" = vapply(yrs, function(y) cnt("PubMed", "AI", y), ""),
  "Europe PMC papers" = vapply(yrs, function(y) baseOf("Europe PMC", y), ""),
  "Europe PMC: ML" = vapply(yrs, function(y) cnt("Europe PMC", "ML", y), ""), "Europe PMC: AI" = vapply(yrs, function(y) cnt("Europe PMC", "AI", y), ""),
  check.names = FALSE, row.names = NULL
)
folded("Table 18. Items mentioning machine learning (ML) and AI per year, with the number using it in brackets", knitr::kable(tab18, align = "lrrrrrrrrr"))
```

**Conclusions**

- The AI label came first, at PAGE in `r fy("PAGE", "AI")`, but only as a
  label. POPKAN, a Bayesian population PK program, was presented as "an expert
  system".
- "Artificial intelligence" for a method of the authors' own appears in PubMed
  in `r ty("PubMed", "artificial intelligence")`, for a regression spline
  method the authors call AI. At PAGE it appears in
  `r ty("PAGE", "artificial intelligence")`, for a deep learning framework.
- In 2024 to 2026, `r pct(aiShare("PAGE", "ML", 2024:2026))` of PAGE abstracts
  mention machine learning, against
  `r pct(aiShare("PAGE", "ML", 2016:2019), 1)` in 2016 to 2019.
- In 2024 to 2026, `r pct(aiShare("PAGE", "AI", 2024:2026))` of PAGE abstracts
  mention AI, against `r pct(aiShare("PAGE", "AI", 2016:2019), 1)` in 2016 to
  2019.
- In the Europe PMC full text of 2024 to 2026,
  `r pct(aiShare("Europe PMC", "ML", 2024:2026))` of the papers mention machine
  learning.
- The only use of either group in the FDA reviews is nonclinical. For Nereus
  (2025) the applicant compared metabolite toxicity in silico with a workflow
  built on a large language model, and the reviewers questioned it.

**Discussion.** These are mentions and uses in what is published, and
publication lags the work. They also come from pharmacometric publications
only. A machine learning paper on drug concentrations that does not use the
core set's search terms is not in the PubMed or Europe PMC base set, so the
literature series understate the wider field.

Europe PMC's open-access full text is thin before about 2010, so its first
years are late by construction. PAGE, with every abstract since 1992, gives
the best dating. Europe PMC also counts a term anywhere in the text, the
introduction included, which is why its mention shares are the highest.

The analysis-type counts in Table 8 and in the machine learning row of
Table 15 measure something narrower. They count machine learning as the type
of the analysis, in items with an estimation tool.

Europe PMC's own search also reaches reference lists and declarations.
`r epBackOnly` Europe PMC records that it returned name no term in the text
searched here, and they are not counted. Most of them have the term only in
the reference list or in a statement about the use of generative AI.
